venues.name: 230 Fifth Rooftop
venues.type: NYC's largest rooftop bar (33,000 sq ft) + indoor lounge; winter igloos November–April
venues.music: DJs Thursday–Saturday plus Sunday brunch; weeknights are lounge-paced, weekends run 80s/90s/house
venues.hours: Roughly noon–1:30am weekdays, later Fri–Sat (the venue's own site lists two conflicting hour sets — call to confirm late hours)
venues.cover: Walk-ins welcome. $15 cover Friday & Saturday from 8pm; $35 skip-the-line option (official)
venues.dress: Official line: “Wear what you love. But no sweatpants or gym clothes.” Weekend nights stricter (reported): no athletic wear or hoodies
venues.age: All ages with a parent EXCEPT Friday & Saturday after 7pm (effectively 21+ at night); government ID required
venues.tables: Groups of 10+ book via SevenRooms up to 30 days out
venues.peak: Summer sunsets; Saturday brunch-to-late; heated igloos make winter a real season here
venues.howto: Just show up — walk-ins are the model. Reservations only for parties of 10+ (a prix-fixe minimum can apply). Skip-the-line tickets on Eventbrite for weekend peaks.
venues.honest: Huge, unpretentious, and openly tourist-friendly — the Empire State Building view is the product. Locals treat it as the bring-your-visitors rooftop; weekends get conveyor-belt crowded and the drinks are ordinary for the price. The winter igloos (and free red Snuggies) are a genuinely fun gimmick.

venues.name: Attaboy
venues.type: No-menu bespoke cocktail bar (~28 seats) at the old Milk & Honey site
venues.music: Low-key bar atmosphere
venues.hours: Daily, 5pm–3am — one of the latest-closing craft cocktail bars in NYC
venues.cover: No cover; cocktails ~$20, bartender's choice (describe a mood or spirit)
venues.dress: None published
venues.age: 21+, valid physical government-issued ID required
venues.tables: Limited OpenTable reservations; otherwise first-come
venues.peak: Waits of 30–60+ minutes at weekend peak; early evening and late-late are the windows
venues.howto: Knock on the unmarked door at 134 Eldridge. Limited reservations now exist on OpenTable (parties of 6 or fewer); everyone else is first-come — on busy nights they take your number and text when seats open. Go 5–7pm or after midnight.
venues.honest: Some of the best drinks in the city with genuinely warm service — the price is the line, the squeeze, and a $20+ gamble on a no-menu pour that almost always pays off. (NYC original only; the Nashville outposts are separate.)

venues.name: Beauty & Essex
venues.type: Glam multi-room restaurant/lounge behind a functioning pawn-shop front (Tao Group)
venues.music: Lounge/party playlist; weekend nights get loud and scene-y
venues.hours: Closed Mon; Tue–Wed 5–10pm; Thu 5–11pm; Fri–Sat 5pm–12am; Sun 5–10pm
venues.cover: No cover — it's a restaurant/lounge. Small plates add up fast; $78/pp tasting menu offered
venues.dress: None enforced; smart casual recommended — the weekend crowd dresses up
venues.age: All ages for dining; 21+ to drink
venues.tables: OpenTable/Resy for dining; larger parties by email
venues.peak: Weekend evenings turn party-loud; weeknights are calmer for the reveal-moment dinner
venues.howto: Walk through the pawn shop at 146 Essex to the hidden staircase. Bar/lounge areas take walk-ins; dining rooms via OpenTable/Resy (bookable 45 days out; parties of 15+ by email).
venues.honest: The pawn-shop reveal and chandelier staircase still land for dates and birthdays — but go for the scene, not the food, which recent reviews call loud, touristy, and overpriced.

venues.name: Bossa Nova Civic Club
venues.type: ~140-capacity fog-heavy techno bar/club under the M-train overpass, open since 2012 (reopened after a 2022 fire)
venues.music: Techno, house, electro, experimental — underground and local-first, no EDM; live hardware sets and occasional touring guests
venues.hours: Open roughly 7 nights, about 7pm–4am (reported via listings; the official site publishes minimal info)
venues.cover: Free on many weeknights and early hours; typically ~$10–$15 cash at the door, more for special lineups (reported). Mostly a door-cash operation with limited advance tickets via RA for bigger nights
venues.dress: None official; all-black/club casual reported
venues.age: 21+ (reported — operates as a bar)
venues.tables: None. No VIP anything.
venues.peak: 1–4am, especially Fri/Sat (reported)
venues.howto: Just show up with cash and a 21+ ID — the door is first-come and rarely selective, but expect a wait after 1am on weekends. Check RA day-of since many nights are free before a certain hour.
venues.honest: The beating heart of cheap, no-frills Bushwick techno — $0–$15 in, decent sound for the size, zero pretense. Downsides: tiny and genuinely cramped at peak, very hot and foggy, bathroom lines, cash-only covers, and quality varies night to night since it's local-DJ-driven.

venues.name: Brooklyn Mirage
venues.type: Former open-air mega-club (part of the Avant Gardner complex, 2017–2024), now rebuilt and rebranded as Pacha New York
venues.music: Was big-room house/techno/EDM; the successor venue Pacha New York books similar large-scale headliners (Justice, Black Coffee, Kaskade)
venues.hours: Not applicable — see Pacha New York for the current venue's schedule (season runs through October 2026)
venues.cover: Not applicable — Pacha New York GA tickets run roughly $50–$130 depending on headliner (official listings, Aug–Sep 2026)
venues.dress: Not applicable
venues.age: The successor venue Pacha New York is 21+ with valid ID (official FAQ)
venues.tables: Pacha New York sells "Backstage" VIP tables from roughly $175–$850 (official)
venues.peak: Not applicable
venues.howto: You can't — the Brooklyn Mirage no longer exists. For events at the same address, see Pacha New York: buy presale at pacha-nyc.com, bring a physical 21+ ID, and expect the highest GA prices in Brooklyn.
venues.honest: The Mirage as people knew it is gone. The timeline: it never reopened after December 2024; parent company Avant Gardner filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in August 2025 with about $155M in debt; the complex sold for roughly $110M; partial demolition followed; and FIVE Holdings (owner of Ibiza's Pacha brand) relaunched the site as Pacha New York on June 20–21, 2026. Roughly $3.1M in unrefunded Mirage tickets were settled with vouchers. If you see "Brooklyn Mirage tickets" on resale sites, they're not real.

venues.name: Death & Co
venues.type: Dark, intimate craft-cocktail institution (est. NYE 2006/07) — one of the bars that launched the modern cocktail renaissance
venues.music: Low-key bar atmosphere
venues.hours: Sun–Wed 6pm–1am; Thu–Sat 6pm–2am
venues.cover: No cover; cocktails $17–26 (most $19–23), zero-proof $17–19, food $10–28
venues.dress: None published
venues.age: 21+ (standard)
venues.tables: SevenRooms reservations or first-come seating
venues.peak: Busy from open; arrive at 6pm sharp or expect 1hr+ weekend waits
venues.howto: Limited reservations for up to 8 via SevenRooms (the old Tock page is dead); walk-ins welcome first-come — put your name down and they text you. No standing room; 2-hour max visit.
venues.honest: Still one of the most reliable world-class cocktail rooms in NYC nearly 20 years in. The trade-offs: the doorstep wait, the strict 2-hour clock, and $20+ drinks in a dim room now firmly on the tourist circuit. (NYC original; LA/Denver/DC branches are separate.)

venues.name: Elsewhere
venues.type: Multi-room live music venue + nightclub (The Hall, Zone One, The Loft, seasonal Rooftop)
venues.music: Indie and underground live acts plus club nights — house, techno, bass, global/Latin
venues.hours: Open most days for events; closes around midnight Mon–Thu, 4am Fri–Sat, 11pm Sun (varies per event)
venues.cover: Tickets via Eventbrite, typically in the $15–$40 range by event (varies widely — check the event page)
venues.dress: No dress code
venues.age: Varies 16+ to 21+ per event — check each show; strict ID rules (US government ID or passport only)
venues.tables: No bottle-table model. Memberships offer perks and discounts; private rentals by email
venues.peak: Friday and Saturday late-night club programming (4am close)
venues.howto: Buy tickets on the official calendar (Eventbrite). No re-entry, mandatory bag checks on big nights. The summer rooftop is first-come and fills at sunset.
venues.honest: Bushwick's tastemaker mid-size venue — three floors plus a beloved summer rooftop, equally credible for indie shows and underground dance nights. Music-first crowd, zero VIP posturing.

venues.name: Employees Only
venues.type: Prohibition-style craft-cocktail bar and late-night New American restaurant behind a psychic's storefront (opened 2004)
venues.music: Art-deco speakeasy vibe; loud and social late, with an in-house psychic doing readings. Burlesque on Sundays (reported)
venues.hours: Daily 6pm–4am with a late kitchen (reported via listings; confirm by phone: (212) 242-3021)
venues.cover: No cover. Cocktails average about $17 with signatures around $20 (reported); mains roughly $22–$30. Dinner reservations by phone only (official); the bar is walk-in
venues.dress: None official; smart-casual reported
venues.age: 21+ to drink; operates as a restaurant so under-21 diners may be possible early (unverified — call ahead)
venues.tables: Dinner tables reservable by phone only (official). Bar seats are first-come
venues.peak: 8pm–midnight nightly; post-midnight becomes an industry hangout, especially weekends (reported)
venues.howto: Call ahead for a dinner reservation if you want a guaranteed seat; otherwise walk in and give your name for the bar. Go before 8pm or after 1am to avoid the crush. Look for the pink neon "Psychic" sign — that's the door.
venues.honest: Still one of the definitive NYC cocktail bars, with the rare virtue of a real 4am kitchen. Downsides: it's been famous for 20+ years, so expect tourists, a crush at the bar on weekends, and hour-plus waits without a dinner reservation.

venues.name: Good Room
venues.type: Two-room club (Good Room main floor / Bad Room side room), open since 2014, with d&b audiotechnik sound
venues.music: House, disco, techno, indie-dance. Residencies: FIXED (JDH & Dave P), The Carry Nation; regulars include Eli Escobar, Justin Strauss, Tim Sweeney, Tony Humphries
venues.hours: Primarily Friday and Saturday, with occasional Thursday/Sunday specials. Doors typically 10pm until roughly 4am (reported — confirm per event on RA)
venues.cover: Tickets via Resident Advisor, reported roughly $10–$30 depending on night and tier; presale cheaper than door (reported — check each RA event page)
venues.dress: None official; casual (reported)
venues.age: 21+ (reported — standard on its RA listings; not stated on venue site)
venues.tables: No bottle-service tables. Private events via goodroomevents@gmail.com (official)
venues.peak: Midnight–3am (reported)
venues.howto: Buy RA presale — door price is higher and popular nights like FIXED or Eli Escobar all-nighters can sell through. The door is generally easy if you're 21+ with ID. Arrive before midnight to skip the line.
venues.honest: One of the most reliable mid-size dance rooms in the city — real DJ bookings, proper sound, unpretentious door. Downsides: the main room gets packed and sweaty at peak, Bad Room can feel like an afterthought on off nights, and the edge-of-Greenpoint location is annoying to reach late.

venues.name: Harriet's Rooftop
venues.type: Rooftop bar/lounge with plunge pool; separate indoor Harriet's Lounge one floor below
venues.music: DJ series: Above(Ten) Saturdays, Sol Together Sundays, Sunset Sessions Fridays
venues.hours: Mon–Thu 12pm–11pm; Fri–Sat 11am–12am; Sun 11am–11pm — weather permitting
venues.cover: No cover stated; entry via reservation or walk-in queue; a suggested 20% gratuity is auto-added
venues.dress: Smart casual (reported): no beachwear or athleisure
venues.age: Minors OK early; commonly reported 21+ in the evening (~9pm cutoff — not official)
venues.tables: Bottle-service packages published from $2,000–$10,000; standard tables via SevenRooms/Resy
venues.peak: Golden hour and summer weekend day-parties
venues.howto: Reserve via SevenRooms or queue. The pool deck loungers are hotel-guests-only, but “Sky Swim Lounge” tables let non-guests buy pool access. Check Instagram for weather closures before you go.
venues.honest: Arguably the best bridge-and-skyline sightline in the city. The costs: $26–31 cocktails, sunset elevator waits, and weather closures that catch people out. The DJ day-parties are the move.

venues.name: House of Yes
venues.type: Performance nightclub & art space (circus, burlesque, themed dance parties)
venues.music: House, disco, eclectic DJ sets; themed costume parties; live variety shows
venues.hours: Dance parties Friday & Saturday (occasionally Thursday), typically until ~4am; event-dependent
venues.cover: Tiered presale tickets, roughly $0–$40+ depending on event; prices rise closer to the date; door entry first-come if not sold out
venues.dress: No formal dress code — themed, creative dress and costumes strongly encouraged (“anything that displays effort will do” per the venue)
venues.age: 21+ for dance parties unless marked All Ages; government photo ID required
venues.tables: Tables via tables.houseofyes.org; group/birthday inquiries by email; minimums not published
venues.peak: Friday and Saturday are the only regular party nights
venues.howto: Buy advance tickets via the official calendar (events frequently sell out). Door tickets only if not sold out. No photos on the dance floor — enforced. Strong consent culture (“Safer Spaces” policy).
venues.honest: NYC's flagship costume-party club — aerialists over the dance floor, themed nights, and a crowd that commits. Expressive and queer-friendly; not a bottle-service scene. Book ahead: the good nights sell out.

venues.name: Knockdown Center
venues.type: Large multi-room events/arts venue in a former glass-and-door factory — concerts, raves, festivals, and the outdoor Ruins courtyard series. Also houses Basement, its strict no-phones techno club
venues.music: House/techno/electronic marquee bookings (Underworld, Sasha, Honey Dijon, Joy Orbison, Horse Meat Disco) plus live rock, hip-hop and indie
venues.hours: Event-driven, concentrated Thu–Sun. Daytime outdoor shows often start 3pm; club nights run late. Doors typically 90 min–2 hrs before showtime (reported)
venues.cover: All tickets via Dice (official FAQ). Typical range roughly $25–$70 depending on the act, with tiered presales cheaper; current listings from ~$43. No refunds except lineup changes (official)
venues.dress: None official; rave/casual standard (reported)
venues.age: Varies by event — most events are 21+, always noted on the event page; valid ID always required (official FAQ)
venues.tables: No table service; GA ticketed events. Lockers available for rent; no re-entry unless specified (official FAQ)
venues.peak: Headliners often after midnight for club shows; outdoor Ruins parties peak late afternoon/evening (reported)
venues.howto: Buy on Dice early — big names sell out and price tiers jump. Check the event page for the age restriction before buying. Budget for a rideshare home or know the Q54/Q59/B57/B38 buses; there's no re-entry, so pack light or rent a locker.
venues.honest: One of NYC's best big-room experiences — multiple stages, serious bookings, plenty of bar capacity. Real downsides: it's a schlep (a 20-minute walk from the Jefferson L per the venue's own FAQ), acoustics get mixed reviews for live-band shows, and sold-out mega-raves mean long lines and a packed floor.

venues.name: Le Bain
venues.type: Penthouse discothèque + rooftop bar (with the famous sunken hot tub)
venues.music: House and disco-leaning; serious DJ residencies (Eli Escobar Wednesdays, Susanne Bartsch Thursdays, François K Sundays)
venues.hours: Mon–Tue 4pm–12am; Wed–Fri 4pm–4am; Sat 2pm–4am; Sun 2pm–12am (summer 2026 schedule; day sessions on weekends)
venues.cover: No cover — the venue states in writing there's no cover for standing room and bar service. Tables optional with minimum spends
venues.dress: Dress-to-impress; no sportswear, jerseys, or hats; discretionary door that gets harder late (reported — not published officially)
venues.age: 21+ (reported)
venues.tables: Optional tables with minimum spends, booked through Resy
venues.peak: Wednesday–Saturday from 10pm for club nights; weekend sunsets for the rooftop
venues.howto: No reservation needed for the floor — but the weekend door is selective and lines get long after 11pm. Tables via Resy. Sunset sessions from 2–4pm on weekends are the easy way in.
venues.honest: The most credible actual club on Manhattan's rooftop circuit — real DJ bookings, a fashion-y, queer-friendly crowd, and free entry traded against a hard, arbitrary door. The hot tub is real.

venues.name: Magic Hour Rooftop Bar & Lounge
venues.type: 10,000 sq ft indoor/outdoor hotel rooftop (Tao Group) — an "urban amusement park" with carousel seating, mini-golf, and rotating seasonal themes
venues.music: DJs and a party-lounge crowd at night; brunch by day; Empire State Building views
venues.hours: Mon–Wed 5pm–12am; Thu 5pm–2am; Fri 5pm–4am; Sat 11:30am–4am; Sun 11:30am–12am. Brunch Sat–Sun 11:30am–3:30pm (official, fetched 2026-08-25)
venues.cover: No general cover and no fee to reserve (official FAQ; card required to hold, $30 no-show fee). Table minimums apply after 9pm Wed–Sat (reported, amounts vary). Cocktails ~$18–$22 (reported)
venues.dress: Official: "fun, casual, no true athletic wear." No shorts/sandals after 9pm (reported)
venues.age: 21+ at all times except weekend brunch (Sat–Sun 11:30am–3pm). Physical government ID required; foreign ID needs a passport (official)
venues.tables: Book via the official widget on moxytimessquare.com; 90-minute table blocks; cancel by noon day-of or $30 fee. Walk-in table service first-come; groups 15+ via events team (official)
venues.peak: Sunset golden hour (~6–8pm) and Fri/Sat 10pm–1am; weekend brunch slammed in summer (reported)
venues.howto: Reserve a table on the official booking widget (free, card hold) especially Thu–Sat; otherwise arrive before sunset and walk in to the bar. After 9pm Wed–Sat expect table minimums — confirm when booking. Bring physical 21+ ID; skip gym clothes.
venues.honest: The views and theme-park set pieces genuinely deliver for photos, and the seasonal takeovers keep it fresh. Downsides: it's a tourist-heavy Times Square scene with resort-level drink prices, 90-minute table limits, and a long weekend door line — locals treat it as a one-time novelty, not a regular.

venues.name: Marquee New York
venues.type: Flagship big-room nightclub (Tao Group)
venues.music: EDM and open-format headliner DJs; Wednesdays lean open-format/hip-hop
venues.hours: Wednesday, Friday, Saturday — 11pm–4am
venues.cover: Cover typically reported around $30–$70 depending on the night and DJ (third-party estimates; exact pricing per event on Tao's ticket pages)
venues.dress: Upscale nightlife attire; enforced, selective door (reported — Tao does not publish a code)
venues.tables: VIP tables via SevenRooms; minimums not published officially (third-party sites quote roughly $1,500+ — unverified)
venues.peak: Saturday headliners; Wednesday is the industry/local night
venues.howto: Tickets via taogroup.com. A “Table Share Experience” product includes admission at a shared table. Expect a line and a selective door — dress up and arrive before peak.
venues.honest: The archetypal Manhattan mega-club, freshly renovated — expanded dance floor, upgraded LEDs, A-list DJs, and a dressed-up bottle-service crowd. Long lines, selective door, expensive drinks: it's a splurge night, not a dive.

venues.name: Mr. Purple
venues.type: Rooftop bar/lounge + restaurant with two terraces and a seasonal rooftop pool
venues.music: DJs on weekend nights and day parties
venues.hours: Mon–Thu 1pm–2am; Fri–Sat 1pm–4am; Sun 2pm–2am
venues.cover: No stated cover; walk-ins welcome. Weekend nights are door-managed; seating at night effectively means bottle service (reported)
venues.dress: Official: “upscale and fashionable” attire, admission at the door host's discretion — enforcement is real on weekend nights
venues.age: 21+ at night (reported — not published)
venues.tables: Via SevenRooms; bottle service for night seating
venues.peak: Sunset, and Friday–Saturday nights; the pool terrace is the summer scene
venues.howto: Walk in early or book via SevenRooms. After 10pm Friday–Saturday expect a line and standing room only unless you reserve a table.
venues.honest: The LES scene rooftop — relaxed and great-value by day, young and packed by weekend night, when it's long lines and standing unless you buy bottles.

venues.name: Musica Club NYC
venues.type: 25,000 sq ft three-level nightclub: Whisper Room lounge, main floor, open-air rooftop over the Hudson
venues.music: House/EDM main room plus hip-hop, Latin, open-format nights and celebrity afterparties
venues.hours: Friday & Saturday, 10pm–4am (per 2026 listings); special events other nights
venues.cover: Tickets via promoters (MTS Productions and event pages), typically ~$20–60 GA, more for celebrity events (unverified — no official price page)
venues.dress: Upscale club standard reported: collared shirts, no athletic wear or sneakers (dated third-party info)
venues.tables: Bottle service via promoters; official booking channel currently unclear
venues.peak: Saturday
venues.howto: Through event promoters and ticket pages — the club's own site is down, so find the current event on MTS Productions or the event's ticket link, and confirm the night is on.
venues.honest: Hell's Kitchen's mega-club heir to the Space Ibiza NY room — big production, a Hudson-view rooftop, and a run of celebrity afterparties. But its own web presence is in disarray: confirm the event before making the trip.

venues.name: Nebula
venues.type: 11,000 sq ft big-room nightclub (~800 capacity, 35 bottle-service tables)
venues.music: EDM and house headliners Friday–Saturday; “Nebula Tuesdays” weekly party leans open-format
venues.hours: Tuesday, Friday, Saturday — 11pm–4am
venues.cover: GA tickets roughly $20–$60 by event, sold via Speakeasy (linked from the official site)
venues.dress: Upscale and enforced (reported): collared shirts/dress shoes for men; no athletic wear, shorts, jerseys, or distressed sneakers
venues.tables: VIP reservations via the official site; birthday packages available; minimums not published (third-party quotes ~$1,000–$2,000+ — unverified)
venues.peak: Friday and Saturday headliner nights
venues.howto: Buy tickets through the official site's Speakeasy links. The door favors dressed-up groups; arrive before midnight on headliner nights.
venues.honest: The biggest club to open in Midtown in years — a polished, LED-heavy, Vegas-style room near Times Square. Draws tourists, birthday crews, and EDM fans; strict door and premium bottle pricing are the recurring themes.

venues.name: Nowadays
venues.type: Indoor/outdoor club, bar and yard run by the Mister Saturday Night crew (Justin Carter & Eamon Harkin)
venues.music: House, techno, leftfield/eclectic. Flagship parties: Mister Sunday (outdoors, Sundays), Nonstop (24-hour party, Saturday 10pm into Sunday), plus a resident-DJ program
venues.hours: Outdoors: Thu 5pm–12am, Fri 5pm–3am, Sat 2pm–3am, Sun 3pm–9pm (Mister Sunday, ticketed). Indoors: Fri 10pm–~6am, Sat 10pm continuously through Sun 10pm for Nonstop (official summer 2026 schedule)
venues.cover: Official guidance: covers vary but tend to be around $25; tickets/RSVP via RA. Official sliding-scale policy: email hello@nowadays.nyc a few days ahead if cover is a barrier — free or reduced entry offered
venues.dress: None official; casual
venues.age: 21+ for nighttime parties (reported via RA listings); daytime outdoor sessions are more open (unverified)
venues.tables: None — no bottle service. Private events: events@nowadays.nyc
venues.peak: Fri/Sat 1–4am indoors; Mister Sunday late afternoon (reported)
venues.howto: Buy RA tickets in advance for Friday/Saturday and Mister Sunday — walkups get turned away when sold out. The door briefs you on consent and phone rules; don't film on the floor. If money is tight, the email-ahead sliding scale is real.
venues.honest: The best-run dance space in NYC for actually dancing — strict no-phones and no-photos rules on the floor, great sound, free water and earplugs. Downsides: the etiquette rules read as preachy to some, covers plus fees add up, Friday/Saturday sells out, and the yard is rough dirt and gravel underfoot.

venues.name: Ophelia Lounge
venues.type: Art Deco rooftop cocktail lounge (1928 tower) — supper-club vibe, not a club
venues.music: DJs on some late nights (“Late Night” programming)
venues.hours: Mon–Wed 5pm–11pm; Thu 5pm–12am; Fri–Sat 5pm–2am; Sun 12pm–11pm
venues.cover: No cover; table-service lounge with happy-hour (“Social Hour”) and prix-fixe offerings
venues.dress: Smart casual leaning dressy (reported — nothing published)
venues.age: Not published
venues.tables: OpenTable reservations; window tables may require minimums
venues.peak: Sunset/golden hour; mostly enclosed, so it works year-round
venues.howto: Book on OpenTable or walk in — window-adjacent tables can carry minimums. Golden hour is the moment.
venues.honest: Date-night and special-occasion territory — a knockout Art Deco room with East River views. More civilized than clubby; pricey cocktails and occasionally slow service are the gripes.

venues.name: Pacha New York
venues.type: Mega-club — open-air main stage (seasonal, roughly June–October) plus indoor Great Hall
venues.music: Big-room house, tech house, melodic techno, afro house, EDM (recent bookings: Kaskade, Justice, Black Coffee, GORDO, ZHU)
venues.hours: Event-driven, mostly Thursday–Sunday, 10pm–4am
venues.cover: GA tickets $50–$130 depending on headliner; “Backstage” VIP from $175–$850 per person — listed directly on the official site
venues.dress: Not published — Mirage-era crowds were casual/rave attire (unverified for the Pacha era)
venues.age: Check each event page — headline events have been 21+ (not centrally published)
venues.tables: “Book Backstage” via vip.pacha-nyc.com — per-person pricing published; full table minimums not published
venues.peak: Saturday headline shows; open-air season peaks June–October
venues.howto: Tickets on pacha-nyc.com (“no hidden fees”). Saturday headliners sell out first — the Aug 29, 2026 show sold out GA and VIP. The venue runs a dedicated shuttle; check the site for transport.
venues.honest: The Brooklyn Mirage's massive open-air successor, relaunched under the Ibiza Pacha brand after Avant Gardner's 2025 bankruptcy. Premium pricing, huge production, heavy demand — and a venue still proving itself to regulators and the neighborhood after the Mirage-era chaos.

venues.name: Paragon
venues.type: Midsize dance club and bar with weekend-only electronic programming
venues.music: Techno, house, drum & bass, Jersey club. Parties include Pressure (Kevin Saunderson), Phantasma, Paradiso, Club Stars
venues.hours: Weekend events only (Fri/Sat, some Sundays), typically ~10pm–4am; event-dependent (reported)
venues.cover: Tickets reported $28–$45; tiered presales on RA/Dice cheaper than door (reported). Official site: RSVP required to enter
venues.dress: No official dress code; casual Bushwick club attire reported
venues.age: 21+ with valid state-issued ID (official)
venues.tables: No bottle-service program advertised; private rentals available (official). Entry is ticket/RSVP-based
venues.peak: Midnight–3am Fri/Sat (reported)
venues.howto: Buy advance tickets on RA or Dice — walk-up without an RSVP is explicitly not allowed. Bring a physical 21+ state ID and arrive before midnight on big nights.
venues.honest: A respected mid-size room with a genuinely good sound system and credible bookings, now with real Detroit techno lineage behind it. Downsides: weekend-only, programming consistency is still re-establishing after the 2025 closure/reopening, and headline nights sell out. It's a music-first room — don't come for bottle service.

venues.name: PHD Rooftop Lounge
venues.type: Rooftop club-lounge (Tao Group) with retractable canopy — bottle-service driven
venues.music: Top 40, hip-hop, EDM (reported)
venues.hours: Wednesday–Saturday, 10pm–4am (closed Sun–Tue)
venues.cover: GA cover reported from ~$50; guest-list/promoter culture is heavy (third-party figures — Tao doesn't publish pricing)
venues.dress: Upscale nightlife attire (reported): collared shirts/dress shoes for men; no sneakers, athletic wear, or hats
venues.age: 21+ (reported)
venues.tables: Tables reported from ~$1,000+ minimum, bottles from ~$525 (third-party, unverified)
venues.peak: Thursday–Saturday from 11pm
venues.howto: VIP tables via SevenRooms; GA often via promoters and ticket sites. Without a table, expect a selective door and a wait after 11pm.
venues.honest: Classic bottle-service rooftop — Empire State views and a scene-y Top-40 crowd. Reviews consistently cite steep covers, pushy table minimums, and a selective door. Go with a table or a plan B.

venues.name: Please Don't Tell (PDT)
venues.type: The genre-defining modern speakeasy (est. 2007) — tiny, dark cocktail den
venues.music: Low-key bar atmosphere; no DJs
venues.hours: Daily until 2am; opens 4–5pm depending on the day
venues.cover: No cover; cocktails around $20
venues.dress: None published
venues.age: 21+ with physical government ID
venues.tables: Resy only; no standing room
venues.peak: Reservations evaporate; walk-in bar seats go within minutes of opening
venues.howto: Resy reservations for 1–8 guests release on a rolling basis up to 7 days ahead — book exactly 7 days out; it rates “very hard” to get. A few first-come bar seats for parties of 4 or fewer go at opening. No standing room. $15/person late-cancel fee.
venues.honest: The phone-booth entrance is still real and still backed by world-class cocktails — but the room is tiny, hard to book, and thick with tourists hunting the booth. Spontaneous visits fail unless you hit the door at opening.

venues.name: Public Records
venues.type: Multi-space venue (est. 2017): hi-fi Sound Room with custom OJAS sound system, Atrium restaurant/venue, UPSTAIRS listening bar, and the seasonal open-air Nursery
venues.music: Deep/dub techno, house, ambient, jazz and global bookings — recent names include Leon Vynehall, Erol Alkan, upsammy, Benji B
venues.hours: Events roughly Wed–Sun. Sound Room club nights typically 10pm–4am; Nursery daytime parties on Sundays (seasonal through ~October). Full weekly hours not confirmed on an official page (reported)
venues.cover: Dice tickets: free to ~$42 all-in. Most Sound Room nights start around $22 first tier rising to ~$32; live shows ~$27–$37; big Nursery all-day events ~$42 (fees-included Dice prices, 2026-08-25)
venues.dress: None official (unverified); stylish-casual reported
venues.age: Sound Room nights reported 21+; restaurant and cafe spaces all-ages (reported)
venues.tables: No club tables. Atrium restaurant takes dinner reservations; UPSTAIRS is partly walk-in (reported)
venues.peak: Fri/Sat midnight–3am in the Sound Room; Nursery Sundays sell out in summer (reported)
venues.howto: Everything sells on Dice — buy the early tier (saves about $10) and use Dice's waiting list for sold-out shows; it works. The door is friendly with no dress-code drama. For summer Nursery daytimes, buy the moment they're announced.
venues.honest: Arguably the best-sounding room in NYC and genuinely adventurous booking, but it's the most polished of the underground venues — drinks are pricey, the crowd can skew fashion/media, and the Sound Room is small enough that floor space disappears fast. Gowanus is a dead zone for late-night transit.

venues.name: Somewhere Nowhere
venues.type: Two-level rooftop lounge + nightclub with seasonal rooftop pool
venues.music: Open-format / hip-hop / house party mix, event-dependent; jazz-leaning after-work programming
venues.hours: Wed 5pm–1am; Thu 12pm–11pm; Fri–Sun 12pm–4am (nightlife runs late Fri–Sun)
venues.cover: GA (arrive before 1am) and Bar Reservation tiers (entry + 4 drink tickets, arrive before 3am) sold via the venue's Weekly Events page; typically ~$20–$50 per third-party listings (unverified)
venues.dress: Smart casual, strictly enforced (venue's own wording): no shorts at night, no athletic wear, team logos, pool slides, distressed sneakers, or tank tops
venues.tables: Bottle service via reservations@elgruposn.com or the events page; ~2-hour table slots; $50/person no-show fee on after-work reservations; dollar minimums not published
venues.peak: Friday and Saturday nights (4am close); rooftop pool daylife on summer weekends
venues.howto: Reserve via the Weekly Events page — strongly recommended, bookable 30 days out. Entry backs up after midnight on weekends; the pool deck is daytime programming in season.
venues.honest: Instagram-bait sky-high rooftop — garden décor, skyline views, a pool — that draws a dressed-up date-night and birthday crowd more than serious dancers. Gorgeous views; strict door, pricey drinks, and post-midnight entry backups are the trade.

venues.name: The Back Room
venues.type: Genuine Prohibition-era speakeasy — cocktails in teacups, beer in paper bags
venues.music: DJs Thursday–Saturday 9pm–close; free Monday night jazz (music 9pm–12:30am)
venues.hours: Sun–Mon 6pm–1am; Tue–Thu 6pm–2am; Fri–Sat 6pm–3am
venues.cover: No cover — “Always Free” per the official site
venues.dress: Official code: no baseball hats, no flip-flops, no tank tops (men), no real fur
venues.age: 21+ Sunday–Thursday; 25+ Friday & Saturday (official — and rarely reported anywhere else)
venues.tables: Walk-ins and reservations both accepted
venues.peak: Weekend DJ nights get packed; Monday jazz is the connoisseur move
venues.howto: Find the alley entrance at 102 Norfolk and walk in, or reserve on the site. Check ahead for private-event closures.
venues.honest: One of only two NYC bars that actually operated during Prohibition — real history, free entry, real late hours. Weekends run young, loud, and packed; drinks are solid rather than exceptional.

venues.name: The Box
venues.type: “Theatre of Varieties” — theatrical burlesque/variety nightclub with bottle-service economics
venues.music: Variety/burlesque stage shows roughly every 30 minutes, open-format music between
venues.hours: Wednesday–Saturday, roughly 11pm–4am; dark Sunday–Tuesday
venues.cover: No standard GA cover — reservations are effectively required for entry; without one it's the doorman's call. Table minimums reported around $500+, bottles ~$500–650 (third-party, fluctuates by night)
venues.dress: Dress to impress — formal leaning; no sportswear, sneakers, or hats (reported; the venue's own FAQ answer is “there's only one way to find out…”)
venues.age: 21+ (standard; not published officially)
venues.tables: Via theboxnyc.com/booking or 917-280-5977; ~$500+ minimums reported
venues.peak: Shows run late — this is a midnight-to-4am room
venues.howto: Book a table via theboxnyc.com or phone. Walk-up entry is discretionary — the venue's own formula: “vibe multiplied by style divided by how many people you're with.” Phones and cameras prohibited inside.
venues.honest: Manhattan's last true late-night theatrical spectacle — genuinely transgressive shows in a gorgeous room. Expensive, selectively doored, and phone-free; reviews split between “unforgettable” and “needed therapy after.”

venues.name: The Dead Rabbit
venues.type: Multi-floor Irish pub and world-class cocktail bar (multiple "World's Best Bar" wins): fast, loud Taproom downstairs, refined Parlor cocktail room upstairs
venues.music: Modern Irish pub energy downstairs; seated cocktail-room atmosphere in the Parlor
venues.hours: Taproom: Sun–Thu 11am–2am, Fri–Sat 11am–3am. Parlor: Tue–Sat 5pm–1am, Sun 4pm–12am, closed Mon (official, fetched 2026-08-25)
venues.cover: No cover. Happy hour Sun–Thu 3–6pm & 11pm–2am with $8 Guinness pints, $2 oysters (reported, June 2026); standard cocktails in the high teens (reported)
venues.dress: None official; come-as-you-are pub downstairs, smart-casual typical for the Parlor (reported)
venues.age: 21+ to drink; the pub serves food from 11am — minors policy unverified, ask the venue
venues.tables: Resy for Taproom tables and Parlor seatings (reported bookable 14 days out); walk-ins take the bar
venues.peak: FiDi after-work rush Thu/Fri 5–8pm; weekend afternoons tourist-heavy; prime Parlor slots book out fast (reported)
venues.howto: Book the Parlor on Resy as soon as the window opens (reported 14 days out) for the full cocktail experience; the Taproom is walk-in friendly if you avoid 5–8pm Thursday/Friday. Hit the 3–6pm or 11pm–close happy hour for value.
venues.honest: Deservedly legendary — arguably the best Irish pub and one of the best cocktail programs in America under one roof. Downsides: perpetually mobbed, the Taproom gets shoulder-to-shoulder and loud, and it sits in a corner of FiDi that's dead quiet otherwise, so it's a destination trip for most people.

venues.name: Westlight
venues.type: Rooftop cocktail bar (Andrew Carmellini / NoHo Hospitality) — cocktails and small plates, not a club
venues.music: DJs at occasional “Westlight Presents” events
venues.hours: Mon–Thu 4pm–12am; Fri 4pm–2am; Sat 12pm–2am; Sun 12pm–12am
venues.cover: No cover. Reservations recommended; walk-ins per availability
venues.dress: Smart casual in practice (nothing published)
venues.age: Under 21 admitted until 6pm daily; 21+ after (official)
venues.tables: Standard reservations; “Turf Club” VIP table program for groups
venues.peak: Sunset, and weekend evenings; indoor wraparound windows make it year-round
venues.howto: Book via the official site (SevenRooms) — sunset and weekend slots go fast. Walk-ins queue for the elevator at peak.
venues.honest: Routinely rated among NYC's best rooftop views — a 360° Manhattan panorama from the 22nd floor. It's a cocktail bar, not a party; the costs are premium drinks and sunset crowds.
